create.name: Bernat Font
create.bio:
Bernat Font is a meditation teacher and scholar of early Buddhism based in Barcelona, who teaches in English, Catalan and Spanish. He came to Buddhism as a teenager, first through Tibetan practice, and later turned towards the Pali texts and the Theravāda, with the Burmese meditation master Sayadaw U Tejaniya shaping much of how he practises. He trained as a community dharma leader at Gaia House and then as a teacher with Bodhi College, where Stephen Batchelor was his mentor, and he completed a doctorate at Bristol University in Buddhist Studies. His research on vedanā, the feeling tone of experience, became the book Early Buddhist Hedonism, which reads the early path as one that works with wholesome joy rather than against it.

He leads retreats and online courses for Bodhi College, Gaia House and other European centres, and in 2022 co-founded Espai Sati, a secular Buddhist association that runs practice groups, retreats and courses in Spanish and Catalan. His sessions mix guided practice with close reading of the suttas, delivered with humour and everyday examples, and he has a particular commitment to LGBTQIA+ practitioners, co-leading Rainbow Dharma retreats. He also translates Pali texts into Spanish and, in another life, plays and composes jazz piano.

books.title: Early Buddhist Hedonism: The Role of Spiritual Pleasure in the Pali Discourses
books.author: Bernat Font
books.description: An academic monograph drawn from his Bristol doctorate. It traces a shared pattern of growing pleasure and ease through the jhānas, the awakening factors and mindfulness of breathing, and argues that the early path makes use of our wish to feel good.

courses.title: Not Your Typical Course on Mettā
courses.description: A six-week online course on Sunday afternoons for anyone who has found loving-kindness practice hard to connect with. Each session combines teaching, contemplative exercises, group discussion and questions, rooted in what the oldest Buddhist texts say about mettā. Sessions are recorded.

courses.title: Right Attitude and Open Awareness
courses.description: A weekend online retreat with Gaia House, co-led with Laura Bridgman, on resting in relaxed, continuous awareness rather than forced concentration. The approach draws on the teaching of Sayadaw U Tejaniya, with practice, reflections and time for questions; suitable for all levels.

courses.title: Mettā in the Heart of Daily Life
courses.description: An online 'sandwich retreat' with Bodhi College, co-led with River Wolton, that weaves kindness practice into an ordinary working week. Opening and closing sessions frame daily practice at home.

courses.title: Samyutta: dharma online
courses.description: Monthly Sunday sessions in Spanish run through Espai Sati, balancing study of early Buddhist texts with practice suggestions for daily life. Sessions are recorded for those enrolled in each block, and fees follow a sliding scale.

free_resources.title: “Mind in the middle” - a guided meditation
free_resources.description: A guided sitting recorded at a London Insight Meditation day in February 2026, free to stream on Dharma Seed.

free_resources.title: Bernat Font's Dharma Talks on Dharma Seed
free_resources.description: His archive of more than seventy recorded talks, instructions and guided meditations in English, mostly from retreats at Gaia House and other insight centres.

free_resources.title: Early Buddhism: the Dharma of Pleasure
free_resources.description: A recorded talk on AudioDharma introducing the themes of his research: how joy and ease function as part of the path in the early discourses.

free_resources.title: Bernat Font on AudioDharma
free_resources.description: His speaker page on AudioDharma, with talks and series in Spanish and English, including a secular dharma series given with Martine Batchelor.
